answer: Each identity declares a compute budget of 863 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Because the jetty audit recomputes usage from the reef history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a inexpensive one. A farm running 188 keys as a result pays for 188 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the karst declaration. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
